subject: Usage-driven provisioning adjustment and short-term GPU add for renewal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>
To: Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@wakefield.health>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Usage-driven provisioning adjustment and short-term GPU add for renewal

Hi Brian —

Thanks again for the detailed uptime call last week. We dug into the June telemetry and we see a persistent 22% higher 95th-percentile token throughput compared to the baseline you shared in March. That increase is concentrated in your inter-day peak window (14:00-17:30 ET) and correlates with the new multi-agent routing you rolled out on June 10.

Given your upcoming renewal (WD-43871) and the desire to avoid latency regressions during the next quarter, we recommend a two-part, usage-driven approach:

1) Short-term burst: +4 A100-equivalent GPUs on the Dedicated pool for 6 weeks to absorb the new peak while we validate batching and cache-hit improvements.
2) Renewal amendment: Add a utilization-contingent clause that lets Wakefield scale the committed tranche by +8 GPUs if sustained 90-day 75th-percentile utilization exceeds 70%.

I've attached the June utilization export and a draft addendum that maps the trigger to billing/pricing. Rishi and Sean are cc'd to scope the provisioning lead time and pricing delta.

Next steps: can you confirm by EOD Wednesday whether procurement can approve a temporary add for July-August? If yes, I’ll get operations to reserve the GPUs and circulate the short addendum.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0126

Attachments: wakefield_utilization_jun2027.csv (CSV, 1.2MB), proposed_capacity_addendum_v2.pdf (PDF, 280KB)

From: Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@wakefield.health>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@wakefield.health
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Usage-driven provisioning adjustment and short-term GPU add for renewal

Naomi —

Appreciate the proactive analysis. Two quick clarifications:

- Can you break out the utilization by model family (chat vs. embeddings) and by environment (prod vs. sandbox)? We need to justify the cost to procurement.
- What’s the expected end-to-end latency reduction for the 95th pct at current load if we add the 4 GPUs versus just enabling more aggressive batching?

Procurement wants a one-page cost delta and expected SLA impact to present at Thursday's ops review. If you can get that to me by Wednesday morning we’ll go into the review with momentum.

—Brian
CFO (acting), Wakefield Health
Brian.Lowe@wakefield.health

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 07:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage-driven provisioning adjustment and short-term GPU add for renewal

Brian —

Thanks — attached is the breakout and a one-slide summary for procurement (see proposed_capacity_addendum_v2.pdf). Highlights:

- Utilization split: ~78% of peak token throughput attributed to chat models (gpt-like), 12% embeddings, 10% rerank. Sandbox contributes <4% in the 95th pct window. (see wakefield_utilization_jun2027.csv)
- Expected latency impact: adding 4 A100-equiv GPUs reduces 95th-pct token latency on the busiest routes by ~18-22% with current routing; enabling our batcher-only tuning yields ~8-10% improvement but increases tail variability during sudden surges.
- Cost delta (6 weeks burst): line-item in the attached addendum, net-of-credit play outlined for first month to offset one-time migration ops.

Operational notes for scheduling: Dev, Sean — can you confirm a 72-hour lead time to provision the 4 GPUs in the us-east pool and whether we can enable auto-fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant if sustained latency drops below SLO? I’ve put the HubSpot deal link in the footer for reference.

If Wakefield signs the temporary add, we’ll:
- Reserve capacity within 24 hours of signed email approval
- Flip routing policy for peak windows to use dedicated pool with prefix caching
- Monitor and deliver a 14-day stabilization report with recommended batcher/kv cache settings

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments: wakefield_utilization_jun2027.csv (CSV, 1.2MB), proposed_capacity_addendum_v2.pdf (PDF, 280KB)

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/WD-43871

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Usage-driven provisioning adjustment and short-term GPU add for renewal

Naomi / team —

Quick ops plan and pricing note:

1) Provisioning lead: 72h confirmed for 4x A100-eq in us-east. We’ll allocate as a 2x2 AZ spread to avoid AZ-specific impact.
2) Fallback quantized variant: feasible — adds ~6% quality delta on sensitive rerank routes; need a signed flag in the addendum to allow automatic fallback for the first 2 weeks.
3) Cost/credits: For a 6-week temporary add, finance recommends a 10% one-time credit applied to the first invoice to offset the burst provisioning risk. I’ve sketched the delta in gpu_burst_strategy.xlsx and linked that to the deal.

Naomi: once Brian confirms, ops will submit the provisioning ticket and I’ll attach the Tech Ops runbook. Dev: please pre-stage the batcher tuning change in the canary pool so we can flip with a single config change.

Rishi
Sr. Product Manager, Capacity & Dedicated Services
rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
